newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Minor components of NZ CPI show mixed trend.
newsitem.headline: Minor components of NZ CPI show mixed trend.

text.p: While New Zealand's headline inflation number for March quarter fell 0.3 percent on a quarter-on-quarter basis, data from Statistics New Zealand showed cried services were mainly responsible for the short-term trend.
Details of the other components of the figure showed mixed trends in the economy.
In transportation, both public and private transport costs fell, driven mainly by international airfares. The prices of new and used cars also fell in the quarter, while vehicle insurance costs rose.
Housing costs rose 0.3 percent in the quarter, against 0.7 percent in the December quarter.
Overall tobacco and alcohol prices rose 0.7 percent in March, due mainly to the increase in excise duties on tobacco that came into effect on December 1, 1996.
Apparel costs fell by 1.1 percent, driven by falls in the costs of mens' clothing and footwear, clothing fabrics and children's footwear.
